The Weekend Guide

This Weekend in the Bay

Friday 14 – Sunday 16 August 2026

A closing opera festival in Oakland, two new galleries opening at the de Young on a free Saturday, Nathaniel Dorsky threading 16mm through a projector in Berkeley, and a mushroom art show in the Outer East Bay. Fifty-eight things worth leaving the house for, across the whole Bay.

West Edge Opera closes Free Saturday at the de Young & Legion New moon — dark skies Fri & Sat Four night markets SFJAZZ summer season ends

Top 5 This Weekend

If you only do five things — one from each corner of the calendar.

  1. Matmos: Metallic Life Review
    Sat Aug 15, 8pm · Gray Area, Mission
    An entire album made from the sounds of metal, performed once, with Recombinant Media Labs on visuals.
  2. West Edge Opera: Handel's Rinaldo
    Sat Aug 15, 2pm · Oakland Scottish Rite Center
    Handel as a comic book, and SF Classical Voice's favourite thing in the festival. Final performance — and The Turn of the Screw follows at 8pm in the same hall.
  3. Five Films by Nathaniel Dorsky, in person
    Sun Aug 16, 1:30pm · BAMPFA, Berkeley
    Silent 16mm at 18 frames a second, with the greatest living Bay Area avant-garde filmmaker in the room. He's also there Friday night.
  4. The Soiled Dove
    Fri & Sat, doors 7:30pm · The Big Top at Alameda Point
    Vau de Vire's Barbary Coast dinner-circus under a 12,000-square-foot big top — new story this season, and Joan Baez back with the cast.
  5. FACT/SF Summer Dance Festival
    Fri & Sat 7:30pm, Sun 3pm · ODC Theater, Mission
    Six world premieres and restagings chosen from a national pool. The Chronicle promised everything from eloquent to absurd, including a raw chicken.

Big Museums

Exhibits, after-hours & museum one-offs

TOP PICK✦ Opening weekend

A Gallery of Their Own: Women Artists from the Carr and Goldblum Gift

Opens Sat Aug 15 · Tue–Sun 9:30am–5:15pm

de Young Museum · Golden Gate Park San Francisco

A whole new gallery given over to women artists from a promised gift — Louise Bourgeois, Lee Krasner, Yayoi Kusama — debuting on the museum’s free-admission day.

Included with admission — free Saturdays for Bay Area residents

Friday Nights at OMCA with Ashley Mehta + Off the Grid

Fri Aug 14 · 5–9pm

Oakland Museum of California · Lake Merritt, Oakland East Bay

The format you always want: eleven Off the Grid trucks on 10th Street, drinks by the koi pond, live music on the Garden Stage and the galleries open late.

Free to attend (museum ticket for galleries)

✦ Final weekend

Drawn to Venice

Closes Sun Aug 16 · 9:30am–5:15pm

Legion of Honor · Lands End San Francisco

Tiepolo and company on paper — the last three days to see it before it comes down.

Included with admission (free Sat for Bay Area residents)

Organ Concert: Eric Choate on the Spreckels Organ

Sat Aug 15 · 4pm

Legion of Honor, Rodin Gallery · Lands End San Francisco

Bach, Duruflé, Widor and Vierne on the Legion’s Spreckels organ, played by SFCM’s professor of choral and organ music, surrounded by Rodin.

Free with admission — and admission is free Saturdays for Bay Area residents

★ CRITICS' · 7x7 · Mission Local

The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy

Through Sep 20 · 9:30am–5:15pm

Legion of Honor · Lands End San Francisco

The largest US showing of Etruscan material ever assembled — about 150 objects from 28 lenders including the Vatican, much of it never out of Italy before.

Ticketed

✦ First US retrospective

Lotty Rosenfeld: Disobedient Spaces

Opened Aug 12 · Wed–Sun

BAMPFA · Downtown Berkeley East Bay

The first US retrospective for the Chilean feminist artist who spent decades marking crosses on roadways to contest the militarization of public space.

Museum admission

Video Craft — closing weekend, with Craft + Chat

Demetri Broxton: Ancestral Echoes — Crops of Empire

Closes Sun Aug 16 · Sat 11–6, Sun 12–5

Museum of the African Diaspora · SoMa San Francisco

Beadwork, cowrie and boxing gloves built into an altar of the crops that built empires — the Oakland artist’s first museum show, ending Sunday.

✦ Saturday only

Bay Model Visitor Center

Sat Aug 15 · 9am–4pm (closed Sun & Mon)

US Army Corps of Engineers · Sausalito North Bay

A 1.5-acre hand-built hydraulic working model of the entire Bay and Delta, in a Marinship warehouse. Saturday is the only day it opens this weekend.

Galleries & Artist Spaces

Openings, receptions, closing days

In Populated Air — opening reception

Fri Aug 14 · 6–8pm

KARL, 50 Francisco St · North Waterfront San Francisco

Eight artists — Stella Zhang, Devynn Barnes, Jan Meissner and others — on inherited and performed stories, built out from a 1980 Lucille Clifton poem. Opening night of a run into October.

Isabella Kirkland: Critters + Patricia Piccinini

Hosfelt Gallery, 260 Utah St · Design District San Francisco

Classical, Opera & Jazz

A festival ends, a season capstone, and jazz in small rooms

TOP PICK★ CRITICS' · SF Classical Voice✦ Final performance

West Edge Opera: Handel’s Rinaldo

Sat Aug 15 · 2pm (2h10)

Oakland Scottish Rite Center, 1547 Lakeside Dr · Lake Merritt, Oakland East Bay

Handel’s crusaders-and-sorcery spectacle staged as a graphic novel, with countertenor Kyle Tingzon in a blue cape. SF Classical Voice called it "a superhero romp with heart." Final performance.

$22–$182

★ CRITICS' · SF Classical Voice✦ Closing night

West Edge Opera: Britten’s The Turn of the Screw

Sat Aug 15 · 8pm (2h45)

Oakland Scottish Rite Center · Lake Merritt, Oakland East Bay

"Opera at its most chilling," per SFCV — Mark Streshinsky’s cinematic staging of the ghost story, closing night. Pair it with Rinaldo at 2pm for a full opera day in one building.

$22–$182

✦ Festival finale

West Edge Opera: American Apollo (Damien Geter)

Sun Aug 16 · 2pm (2h30)

Oakland Scottish Rite Center · Lake Merritt, Oakland East Bay

A contemporary opera about John Singer Sargent and Thomas McKeller, the Black hotel worker who modeled for his murals and went uncredited. Directed by Nataki Garrett; the festival’s closing performance.

Theater

World premieres, closing weekends and free Shakespeare

TOP PICK★ CRITICS' · SF Chronicle

Iphigenia in Splott

Fri & Sat 8pm · Sun 2pm (audio-described)

Shotgun Players, Ashby Stage, 1901 Ashby Ave · Berkeley East Bay

Gary Owen’s solo tour de force — Effie, foul-mouthed and self-possessed in a Welsh town, turning into a modern Iphigenia. Shotgun’s first one-person show in 34 years; the Guardian put it among the 50 best plays of the century.

$25–$80 sliding scale

✦ World premiere · waitlist only

The Prince, Parts 1 & 2 — world premieres

Part 1: Fri 7pm & Sun 5pm · Part 2: Sat 7pm

Central Works, Berkeley City Club, 2315 Durant Ave · Berkeley East Bay

Gary Graves’s two-play cycle on Machiavelli — Savonarola, Cesare Borgia, and the invention of political realism — playing in rotation in a 1927 Julia Morgan clubhouse. Central Works’ 80th and 81st world premieres.

$35–$45

WRECKAGE: A Musical Tragicomedy

Sat Aug 15 · 2pm (live music from 1:30)

Glen Park, Chenery & Elk St · Glen Park San Francisco

The SF Mime Troupe’s 67th season: hallucinating robots, economic collapse and protesting frogs, played on a portable stage in a public park for nothing.

Free

Red Morton Park · Redwood City South Bay

Dance

Six world premieres, a 1997 landmark restaged, and Deaf dance

TOP PICK★ CRITICS' · SF Chronicle✦ Six world premieres

FACT/SF 2026 Summer Dance Festival

Fri & Sat 7:30pm · Sun 3pm

ODC Theater, 3153 17th St · Mission San Francisco

Six pieces — a mix of world premieres and restagings — chosen from a national pool, by FACT/SF, Ishami Dance Company, Karla Quintero, Sonam Tshedzom Tingkhye and others. The Chronicle promised "eloquent to absurd," including a raw chicken.

Ticketed via ODC

✦ First restaging since 1997

ICE. CAR. RAGE.

Fri, Sat & Sun · 8pm (~45 min)

Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture · Marina San Francisco

The first restaging of Jess Curtis, Keith Hennessy and Jules Beckman’s 1997 landmark — an autonomous car, a block of ice and a gilded cage. Closes Gravity’s season honoring Curtis. The exhibition Please. Stay. Touch. is open in the same building and ends Sunday.

Ticketed; only 40 chairs, otherwise standing

✦ Once a year

14th Bay Area International Deaf Dance Festival

Fri & Sat 7:30pm · Sun 1–4pm outdoors

Dance Mission Theater (Fri/Sat) · Presidio Tunnel Tops (Sun) · Mission / Presidio San Francisco

Antoine Hunter brings Deaf and hard-of-hearing artists from across the country to a favorite Mission venue, then out onto the Tunnel Tops lawn for free on Sunday. Saturday adds live captions and an audio-description and haptic tour.

Indoor ticketed; Sunday free with RSVP

Small, strange, and mostly gone by Monday

Fri & Sat · doors 7:30pm, show 8pm

✦ Free, and clear this weekend

Free Telescope Viewings on the historic refractors

Fri & Sat · 7:30–10:30pm

Chabot Space & Science Center, 10000 Skyline Blvd · Joaquin Miller Park, Oakland East Bay

Leah (1883), Rachel (1916, the largest refractor in the West open to the public) and Nellie, 1,500 feet above the Bay. The new moon was Aug 12 and the forecast is partly cloudy and dry — genuinely dark after 9:30. Check the humidity gate before you drive up.

Free

Literary & Ideas

Salons, readings and one very good documentary

TOP PICK✦ Sold out

Robert Hass and Brenda Hillman: A Third Commonness

Fri Aug 14 · 7–8:30pm

Mrs. Dalloway’s, 2904 College Ave · Elmwood, Berkeley East Bay

A Pulitzer winner and former US Poet Laureate on poetry as a relationship between people and land, from Zen Buddhism through California ecopoetics — in conversation with Brenda Hillman. Two major poets, one small room.

Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Ave · Grand Lake, Oakland East Bay

Eva Silot Bravo and Umi Vaughan on Afro-Brazilian sacred drumming under religious persecution and the transnational Cuban alt-music scene. Two artist-scholars in the best small room in Oakland.

Stacy Carlson: The Gyre

Sun Aug 16 · 5–7pm

Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Ave · Grand Lake, Oakland East Bay

A novel about a 19th-century Russian Orthodox monk walking into the Arctic — faith, solitude, folklore, ecology — read with poet Paul Corman-Roberts and framed by anthropologist Cari Borja.

✦ Tiny format

Cybersentics Book Club: "Ghastly Marionettes"

Sun Aug 16 · 12–2pm

Gray Area Incubator, 2665 Mission St · Mission San Francisco

A reading group on Danielle Carr’s essay about how "cognitive liberalism" shaped Cold War psychology and its entanglement with critiques of totalitarianism. History of science and sociology, in a small upstairs room.

San Francisco Rising — screening and director Q&A

Sun Aug 16 · 3–5:30pm (film 3:15, 91 min)

Koret Auditorium, SF Main Library, 100 Larkin St · Civic Center San Francisco

Adam Leao shot this guerrilla-style through 2024 — natural light only, no tripods — following thirty-odd San Franciscans from homeless advocates to transit workers to artists. He takes questions after.

Great Lawn, Yerba Buena Gardens · SoMa San Francisco

Al Green at the Stern Grove Festival — season finale

Sun Aug 16 · 2pm

Sigmund Stern Grove, 19th Ave & Sloat · Sunset San Francisco

A soul legend closing the 89th season of free concerts in a eucalyptus amphitheatre, with Goapele and the Glide Ensemble. KQED called it the free concert of the summer.

✦ 35th annual

Cotati Accordion Festival

Sat & Sun · roughly 9:45am–8pm

La Plaza Park, Cotati · Sonoma County North Bay

Five stages of accordion across two days — a polka tent, a zydeco dance party, a jam tent and an "Apocalypse" alternative stage. 35th year. Absurd and beloved in equal measure.

Notes

Times and dates were read off each venue's own event page wherever possible, not off aggregator grids. Where an aggregator and a venue disagreed, the venue won — that resolved the West Edge Sunday title (American Apollo, 2pm) and caught a Herbie Hancock listing that is actually Monday Aug 17, so it isn't here.

Worth double-checking before you go: Chabot and Foothill telescope nights are cancelled if it's humid — check the day of. Oakland Theater Project doesn't publish curtain times; call 510.646.1126. Both The Prince dates at Central Works show as fully reserved, with a waitlist opening 30 minutes before curtain. Robert Hass at Mrs. Dalloway's is sold out with a waitlist. BAMPFA's Dr. Strangelove and 2001 are sold out. Al Green at Stern Grove needs a free reservation through the lottery.

Deliberately left out: arena and stadium shows, DJ and club nights, beer and food festivals, sports, and — per the standing note for this run — Pride and LGBTQ-specific programming, which this weekend meant Oakland Pride, a Compton's Cafeteria history ride, and YBCA's Conjuring Power.

Scanned across all 15 source categories in the registry, plus critics at the Chronicle, KQED, SF Classical Voice, 48 Hills, Mission Local, SF Standard, 7x7 and Broke-Ass Stuart.
